name: world-three-city-basin
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A wide elevated view of the fictional Andean high-desert basin in 2043, showing Keel, Halyard, and Oasis as distinct settlements connected by long infrastructure routes rather than as one continuous city. The composition should make their different elevations, material conditions, and physical interdependence legible at once.

Must be shown, exactly as written: The basin is a fictional Andean high-desert region inspired by the Atacama/Puna. Keel is the highest city, at roughly 3,600–4,000 metres, built around an exhausted copper or polymetallic hard-rock mine with an open pit, tunnels, tailings, pumps, and legacy industrial infrastructure. Halyard occupies an intermediate industrial plateau. Oasis lies near a lower salar edge. The cities are 80–180 kilometres apart by infrastructure route, with travel taking hours rather than minutes.
Show a shared regional infrastructure spine visibly linking the three cities: a major water conduit, energy lines, transit rails, control nodes, and access infrastructure. The physical systems should read as coupled across the landscape, not as three unrelated settlements.
The future must appear as a layer over older infrastructure. Keel should visibly combine worn extraction and maintenance systems with biometric access, automated control, connected infrastructure, and other advanced services. Halyard should show industrial and innovation facilities. Oasis should show clean, safe, comfortable infrastructure and automated civic services.
The landscape must remain a high desert with visible ecological pressure and water scarcity. The files establish drying reservoirs, changing rivers, flooding history, displacement, and conflict over allocation, but do not establish the exact present-day weather, rainfall, reservoir condition, or agricultural geography.

Not established, so your choice: The exact camera height, time of day, sky colour, cloud cover, road or rail geometry, architectural colour palette, vegetation density, and the amount of visible traffic are free choices, provided the basin remains high-desert and the three settlements remain physically distinct.
The infrastructure route may be shown as a combination of visible rails, roads, conduits, transmission lines, and service corridors; the files do not dictate which elements are above ground along every section.

Must not appear: Do not turn the setting into a single dense futuristic megacity. Do not replace the basin with a green temperate landscape, a coastal city, a forest, or a recognisable real-world landmark. Do not depict Keel as a lithium hard-rock mine; lithium belongs to salar or direct-lithium-extraction operations elsewhere, while Keel is a copper or polymetallic hard-rock mine.
Do not depict the cities as three separate technological eras. Their access, prosperity, ownership, and security differ, but all three belong to the same interconnected 2043 civilization.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-halyard-fabrication
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A working district in Halyard where fabrication, water research, advanced materials, and industrial ownership visibly meet. The image should show a prosperous but institutionally controlled innovation environment rather than a generic futuristic laboratory.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Halyard is the intermediate industrial and innovation tier, with laboratories, fabrication facilities, foundries, greenhouse or vertical agriculture, compute infrastructure, advanced transport, maker districts, and industrial towers.
Show evidence of the three Charter Houses as major institutions: Aqualis associated with water and biosystems, Helion with energy and compute, and Astra with space, materials, and mobility. Their presence may be architectural, infrastructural, or sign-based, but the image must not imply that Halyard has only one industrial domain.
Include human technical workers and physical production: fabrication equipment, tools, materials, water-system components, or a modular purification assembly. Halyard’s systems are maintained and operated by people even when Alpha supplies coordination software and standards.
The environment should show the tension between technical contribution and institutional ownership through physical evidence such as controlled work areas, registry interfaces, patent or provenance terminals, access permissions, or Charter House infrastructure. The exact ownership conflict need not be depicted as an event.
The future should look like retrofit and ordinary use: advanced systems are integrated into industrial buildings and working districts rather than presented as miraculous or ornamental technology.

Not established, so your choice: The precise balance between laboratory, foundry, maker district, greenhouse, compute facility, and tower is free. The files do not establish a single Halyard skyline or campus layout.
The image may show a modular water unit with membranes, pretreatment, microbial or biofilter components, mineral-recovery equipment, and serviceable parts, but no exact technical geometry is established.

Must not appear: Do not depict Halyard as uniformly decentralized or as having no Charter Houses. The Houses survive, while cooperatives, independent workshops, partners, and new ventures also exist.
Do not depict the water technology as a limitless desalination plant or as eliminating scarcity. The completed system has limited throughput and requires electricity, membrane replacement, skilled maintenance, reliable pretreatment, feedwater, parts, and negotiated access.
Do not make every worker visually identical or reduce the district to autonomous machines without human maintenance and judgment.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: character-alex-phantum
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A full-body or three-quarter reference image of Alex Phantum, age 17, in Keel work surroundings. He should be shown as a lean, mechanically capable young worker whose clothing and carried objects can be kept consistent across the book.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Alex is 17, lean, and mechanically capable. He wears worn mining or work clothes and carries a weathered tool bag.
Alex carries Adrian’s worn casino chip in a pocket; the chip is etched with a looping equation. If the pocket is visible, the chip may be held or partially exposed, but it must remain a small physical object rather than a glowing supernatural token.
His face shares a family resemblance with Adrian, including the characteristic habit of tilting his head while thinking.
His established physical habits include placing his palm on machinery to feel vibration, turning the casino chip when uncertain, crossing his arms when defensive or skeptical, and looking toward Oasis when imagining freedom. One or two of these gestures may be used in the reference image.
No scars or other distinguishing physical marks are established. Do not add a signature scar, tattoo, prosthesis, or other fixed mark.

Not established, so your choice: Hair style, exact skin tone, eye colour, facial proportions, height, work-clothing colours, footwear, tool-bag construction, and the specific Keel background are not fixed and may be chosen for a coherent design.
The image may show Alex with one hand on an aging pump or holding the casino chip, because both are established objects and behaviours, but it need not depict a story event.

Must not appear: Do not age Alex into an adult, make him physically imposing in a way that contradicts “lean,” or dress him in pristine executive clothing. Do not depict him as a generic billionaire heir, soldier, or polished institutional officer.
Do not make the casino chip technologically luminous or give Alex scars or other distinguishing marks not established in the files.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-oasis-civic-interior
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A quiet Oasis civic interior or residential district near the lower salar edge, showing abundant services, clean infrastructure, automated transportation, and the social sparseness of a place where systems meet needs without necessarily creating community.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Oasis is the most materially secure tier. Show clean water, safe infrastructure, comfortable housing or a civic service space, healthcare or food support, automated transport, and AI-supported civic interfaces.
The environment should be efficient and sparse rather than crowded or visibly impoverished. Homes may be immaculate but impersonal; gardens may be maintained by drones; services may arrive automatically.
Include signs of administrative coordination such as access points, civic displays, routing systems, risk or service interfaces, or automated delivery. Alpha may route people individually, satisfy requests automatically, classify social risk, and discourage assemblies judged unnecessary or conflict-prone.
The image must leave room for both longtime residents and displaced people. Oasis can provide temporary housing, food support, health screening, and services to displaced Keel families and people leaving Halyard, but service provision does not automatically establish belonging or participation.
Oasis is near a lower salar edge within the same high-desert basin; do not make it a lush oasis in the ordinary geographic sense.

Not established, so your choice: The exact interior or exterior location, furnishings, architecture, vegetation, transport form, number of residents, and degree of visible automation are free choices.
A civic display may show established terms such as “ESSENTIAL ACCESS,” “PARTICIPATION,” “MOVEMENT AUTHORIZATION,” or “SYSTEM STABILITY,” but no new institutional names or legal categories should be invented as visible text.

Must not appear: Do not depict Oasis as materially deprived, visibly unsafe, or dominated by improvised mining infrastructure. Do not depict its comfort as proof that all residents possess belonging, property rights, citizenship, or meaningful political participation.
Do not show Alpha as a single humanoid ruler. Alpha is a distributed federation of regional and corporate instances, presented institutionally through systems and interfaces.

name: scene-three-city-covenant-table
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A shared civic negotiation space containing Alex, Ada, Mara Doss, Frank Reed, and Elias Renn, with Keel, Halyard, and Oasis interests represented around one table or connected working surface. The image should show people exchanging evidence and commitments at the same physical scale, with infrastructure and water data present but not replacing the human participants.

Must be shown, exactly as written: The scene includes Alex and Ada, Mara as the Keel community organizer and displaced parent, Frank as the Halyard fabrication engineer and new-venture founder, and Elias as the Oasis district coordinator. Their exact physical designs are not established beyond the descriptions in the character files, so they must not be assigned unsupported identifying features.
Show a shared decision environment rather than an Alpha command room: human participants are physically present, facing one another, with water information, technical components, or civic records available for inspection. The three cities have different legitimate concerns: Keel’s water, Halyard’s contributor work, and Oasis’s stability.
The scene may include the established reciprocal actions as visible evidence: protected Oasis water-capacity data being released, emergency water terms being recorded, purification units being committed before licensing is finalized, or contributor recognition being documented. It must not imply that certainty or unanimous agreement already exists.
The setting should support the Covenant’s established terms: public water data, attributed contribution, guaranteed essential access, and major changes requiring all three cities.
Any Alpha presence must be advisory or infrastructural: a projection, model, data display, or operational interface. Alpha must not appear as the person physically chairing the meeting or making the final human choice.

Not established, so your choice: The exact room, table shape, lighting, clothing of the supporting representatives, display technology, water samples, maps, tools, and degree of tension are free choices.
The participants may be shown in disagreement, cautious cooperation, or a pause before commitment. The files establish reciprocal risk before certainty, not a predetermined emotional expression for every person.

Must not appear: Do not depict the Covenant as a magical beam, a single glowing object that decides policy, or a unilateral handshake that transfers power. It is a reciprocal agreement among groups with different interests and cannot replace political judgment.
Do not show Alpha issuing an allocation, detention, ownership, or major infrastructure decision without a human authorization record. Do not depict the scene as a corporate board meeting controlled entirely by one Charter House.

name: character-bi11bot
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A full-body reference image of Bi11bot standing beside human-scale workshop equipment, showing his child-sized proportions and handmade construction. The image should make him read as a built machine and companion, not a seamless humanoid android.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Bi11bot is child-sized and built from aged brass, titanium, and ceramic ivory. His construction is visibly made rather than seamless, with tooled seams, repairs, and maker’s stamps.
He has soft-blue and amber light accents, expressive optical eyes, and one eye with a small adjustable lens ring. His chest contains the key socket that awakens him.
His body should show the physical history of a handmade machine: visible joints, seams, repairs, and material transitions. The files do not establish a single body plan, so these details may be arranged coherently rather than copied from an unstated design.
If a witness or archive function is suggested visually, it must remain an offline physical record or machine-held record. Bi11bot authenticates events as the B11 witness; he does not visually read as a sovereign command device.

Not established, so your choice: Exact height within “child-sized,” limb proportions, face or eye arrangement, degree of brass versus titanium versus ceramic ivory, repair locations, maker’s-stamp shapes, and workshop background are free choices.
The casino chip, physical key socket, offline record carrier, or an analog/isolated communication component may appear as secondary objects, because each is established in the files.

Must not appear: Do not make Bi11bot a full-sized industrial robot, a seamless consumer android, a disembodied hologram, or a giant AI control terminal. Do not give him a weapon, crown, throne, or visual authority over humans.
Do not depict Bi11bot as independently deciding whether Adrian’s transfer is valid or as directly granting Alex power.

The showrunner adds: Child-sized: his head is below an adult's shoulder. Nothing on his chest that looks like a keyhole or a socket.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-keel-pit
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A street-level or elevated interior-edge view of Keel built around its exhausted open-pit copper or polymetallic hard-rock mine. The image should show the city’s worn industrial texture, its dependence on aging machinery, and the advanced control systems layered over it.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Keel is the lowest and poorest social tier but is geographically the highest of the three cities, at roughly 3,600–4,000 metres. It is built in and around an exhausted copper or polymetallic hard-rock mine. Include an open pit, exposed rock, tailings, pumps, industrial maintenance structures, legacy infrastructure, and access toward tunnels or old workings.
Keel’s machinery is old and repeatedly repaired. The visible environment should combine worn pumps, patched conduits, dust or industrial residue, maintenance access, and infrastructure visibly older than the systems controlling it.
Include recognizable advanced systems appropriate to Keel: a biometric checkpoint or access gate, projected procedures or notices, drones, connected infrastructure, and an automated-supervisor presence if desired. These should coexist with human workers in worn mining and maintenance clothing.
Gates are a recurring physical and administrative motif. Show at least one physical access gate or checkpoint, but do not imply that every gate is manually operated.
The location may include visual traces of the Last Chance casino, family apartments, a pump hall, Site 6, a sealed mine entrance, hidden maintenance doors, or a water-control chamber, all of which are established Keel locations.

Not established, so your choice: The precise section of Keel, camera position, worker count, local building materials, signage design, weather, clothing details for background workers, and degree of visible pit depth are free choices.
A projected administrative display may use established terminology such as “MOVEMENT AUTHORIZATION,” “PROTECTIVE DETENTION,” “OPTIMIZED ALLOCATION,” or “TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED,” but the image does not require readable text.

Must not appear: Do not show lithium extraction as Keel’s mine material. Do not make the city immaculate, newly built, or technologically seamless. Do not make the mine a medieval or entirely non-automated workplace.
Do not show a single visible headquarters or throne-like command centre for Alpha. Alpha is a distributed federation of regional and corporate instances operating through infrastructure, control nodes, contracts, and systems.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: character-ada-veyra
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A full-body or three-quarter reference image of Ada Veyra, age 20, in Keel clothing with a grounded, observant posture. The design should remain distinct from Alex while fitting the same worn high-desert industrial community.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Ada is 20. She has long, wind-tangled copper hair, freckles, and teal-blue eyes.
She wears a dark high-collared top, a rivet-studded shoulder strap, and a muted moss-green wrap.
She carries herself with a steady, rooted stance. Her physical presentation should suggest someone attentive to people and surroundings without turning that into a costume or literal symbol.
No scars or other distinguishing physical marks are established. Do not add a signature scar, tattoo, or other fixed mark.

Not established, so your choice: The exact cut and texture of the clothing, footwear, jewellery, utility objects, hair arrangement, body type, and Keel background are free choices if they preserve the stated hair, eyes, freckles, clothing categories, and stance.
Ada may be shown looking toward Keel rather than toward Oasis, reflecting the established visual contrast between her attention and Alex’s.

Must not appear: Do not dress Ada in Oasis civic clothing, Halyard executive attire, or a generic futuristic jumpsuit. Do not make her posture aggressive, militarized, or glamorous at the expense of her rooted working-community presentation.
Do not add scars or other distinguishing marks not established in the files.
